hook.say: This morning, the post was about Blueprints AI saying it can generate permit-ready blueprints in minutes and update a full project from one change. I went back in to check the numbers around product scope, market pull, and what rivals already charge.

findings.label: SCOPE
findings.headline: Blueprints AI says V2 saves 300+ hours per project
findings.detail: Company site says a full set is generated in minutes rather than weeks.
findings.say: First, the company now puts a number on the pitch: 300 plus hours saved per project, with a first CD set in about 30 minutes of chat.

findings.label: ADOPTION
findings.headline: Blueprints AI says 4,000+ companies have signed up
findings.detail: That is sign-up volume, not confirmed paid deployment or production usage.
findings.evidence: Join the 4,000+ companies already signed up
findings.say: Second, Blueprints says more than 4,000 companies have signed up. That shows interest, but signed up is not the same as live inside an engineering workflow.

findings.label: PRICE
findings.headline: Sibling product ADU AI sells permit package from $4,950
findings.detail: ADU AI is built by the same founder and compares one-time filing to monthly SaaS.
findings.say: Third, the same founder’s ADU AI sells a permit-ready package at 4,950 dollars one time, while Blueprints AI was reported at 3,200 dollars a month.

take.headline: The real test is workflow fit
take.say: My take: fast generation matters less than where the output lands. Simple, reviewable automation inside the real toolchain beats a smart-looking demo.

sources.title: Mango Developer — Blueprints AI v2 pricing report

caption:
This morning was about Blueprints AI claiming permit-ready blueprints in minutes and shifting time away from drafting.

300+ hours saved per project, according to Blueprints AI.
4,000+ companies signed up, but that is demand, not proven production use.
ADU AI, from the same founder, sells a permit-ready package from $4,950 one time, while Blueprints AI was reported from $3,200 per month.

My take: in engineering, speed only matters if generation, review, and delivery fit the workflow people already run.
